title: Equipment
author: Hendo
description: Equipment from the Cyberpunk 2020 Corebook, with existing site extensions preserved.

fashion.name: Fashion
fashion.description: The clothing styles of 2020 break into five basic fashion statements.

types.Generic Chic: This is the standard streetwear, made up of colorful modular components in many colors. Belts, coats, sashes and boots predominate.
types.Leisurewear: This is the equivalent of 21st-century athletic wear: padded fleece, corporate and athletic logos.
types.Businesswear: This is the equivalent of the standard business suit: understated colors, pinstripes, real leather shoes, etc. Wool and other natural fabrics are considered the proper outfitting for the up-and-coming Corp.
types.High Fashion: Sophisticated and expensive dressing for the upper class. Designer labels include Miyake, Si-fui Yan and Anne Calvin.
types.Urban Flash: Video jackets, colorshift fabrics, cammo, leathers, metal spikes, Logowear, jeans, leather skirts and boots. The wildest and most utterly chilled in cyberfashion.

techscanner.name: Techscanner
techscanner.description: A small handheld microcomputer with various I/O connectors and probes. Techscanners run diagnostic programs, identify and examine malfunctioning components, and display internal schematics on a small screen.

cuttingtorch.name: Cutting Torch
cuttingtorch.description: Common oxyacetylene type out of a bottle. Handheld and about a foot long. More powerful models are available, up to thermite lances at 5 to 15 times the normal cost.

techToolkit.name: Tech Tool Kit
techToolkit.description: Mixed kit of tools for repairing mechanical items, usually in a 4 by 16 by 2 inch case.

eletronicToolkit.name: Electronics Tool Kit
eletronicToolkit.description: A mixed kit of tools for repairing electronic items.

protectiveGoggles.name: Protective Goggles
protectiveGoggles.description: Protective eyewear for welding, metal machining, chemical mixing and similar work.

flashtube.name: Flashlight
flashtube.description: A standard flashlight with a beam range of 100 to 120 feet. Smaller pocket lights with one quarter of the range cost half the normal price.

glowstick.name: Glowstik
glowstick.description: A chemical light in a 6-inch plastic tube. Shake or break it to activate. Its soft light lasts up to six hours and is available in green, blue or red.

flashpaint.name: Flashpaint
flashpaint.description: Fluorescent paint that gives off a soft light equal to a Glowstik and lasts up to four hours.

flashtape.name: Flashtape
flashtape.description: The same material as Flashpaint in tape form. It lasts six hours and comes in a variety of widths.

rope.name: Rope
rope.description: Braided synthetics in a variety of thicknesses and weights. Can hold up to 1,000 pounds.

breathmask.name: Breathing Mask
breathmask.description: A common painter's mask covering the nose and mouth, with two replaceable side filters. Replacement filters cost 1 eb per pack of ten. Good for keeping out the smog.

hologen.name: Holo Generator
hologen.description: A small box, about 4 by 2 by 6 inches, that projects a holographic picture from a replaceable chip. It accepts chips from most digital cameras and can be linked to a digital recorder/player.

videoBoard.name: Video Board
videoBoard.description: A monitor using flat-LCD technology. No thicker than an inch, most are built into TVs, but all have input plugs for use as readout monitors. Large units are used as advertising signs.

dataChip.name: Datachip
dataChip.description: The storage medium of the future. Usually plastic-cased, datachips come as buttons, flat squares and triangular slivers; adapter plugs let any recorder read any shape.

logcompass.name: Logcompass
logcompass.description: A programmable inertial compass that tracks changes in direction from a fixed bearing or point.

digitalRecorder.name: Digital Recorder
digitalRecorder.description: An audio recorder using datachip technology. Most are the size of two paperback books stacked flat, although some are smaller than a pack of cards.

digitalCamera.name: Digital Camera
digitalCamera.description: Digitizes still images onto a chip cartridge. About the size of a pack of cigarettes.

videoCam.name: VideoCam
videoCam.description: Can be headset-mounted, shoulder-mounted or handheld depending on size. Sound and image are normally recorded on a compact tape-pak, or fed directly to a transmitter through cables. The listed price is for the least expensive shoulder-carried model.

tapePlayer.name: Video/Audio Tape Player
tapePlayer.description: Plays VideoCam tape-paks as well as many older-style audio tapes.

tape.name: Video Tape
tape.description: High-density digital media capable of handling both audio and visual images.

pocketTV.name: Pocket TV
pocketTV.description: Uses a flat-scan screen in a package about 5 by 5 by 3/4 inches or smaller and receives most VHF and UHF stations.

chipPlayer.name: Digital Chip Player
chipPlayer.description: Plays audio- and video-recorded chips. A Video Board is required to display a chip's video track.

chip.name: Digital Music Chip
chip.description: Stores one to six music albums in semiconductor and plastic form. Read-write versions are available.

eletricGuitar.name: Electric Guitar
eletricGuitar.description: Lighter and more flexible than the classic axe, sometimes in an unrecognizable shape. Strings and frets may even be replaced by banks of keys.

eletronicKeyboard.name: Electronic Keyboard
eletronicKeyboard.description: Little changed from present-day keyboards except in size and power.

drumSynthesizer.name: Drum Synthesizer
drumSynthesizer.description: A set of percussion pads and a sound box. It fits into a couple of suitcases and can be arranged however the drummer prefers.

laptop.name: Laptop Computer
laptop.description: A common portable with an internal hard drive, detachable Video Board and slots for data or programming chips. It lacks the advanced CPUs and memory of a regular computer and cannot be used for Netrunning.

pocketComputer.name: Pocket Computer
pocketComputer.description: A programmable calculator with keyboard and chip slots, holding up to 100 pages of alphanumeric memory.

interfaceCables.name: Interface Cables
interfaceCables.description: Typical plug-ended splicing cables that connect a cyber-operated machine to a person's Interface Plugs.

lowImpedance.name: Low Impedance Cables
lowImpedance.description: Special low-resistance, low-interference cables for improved data transfer. They grant +1 to interfacing tasks such as controlling cybervehicles or Netrunning.

trodeSet.name: 'Trode Set
trodeSet.description: A low-efficiency headset for piggybacking in the Net. Applies -2 to Interface.

keyboard.name: Keyboard
keyboard.description: Can be connected to a cybermodem or other electronic equipment.

terminal.name: Terminal
terminal.description: A workstation with keyboard, Video Board and I/O connectors. It can be used to Netrun, making the runner immune to most Black software, but applies -5 to Interface. Terminal operators are commonly known as net-tortoises.

mastoid.name: Mastoid Commo
mastoid.description: A radio transceiver glued to the jaw and temple. It transmits by subvocalization and receives through soundless vibrations. Range: 10 miles.

pocketCommo.name: Pocket Commo
pocketCommo.description: A typical small walkie-talkie. Range: 10 miles.

cellularPhone.name: Cellular Phone
cellularPhone.description: Mobile communication anywhere within a radiotelephone transceiver network. Service costs 100 eb per month.

miniCellPhone.name: Mini Cell Phone
miniCellPhone.description: Fits inside a pack of cigarettes.

binglasses.name: Binoglasses
binglasses.description: High-tech vision aids combining binoculars with a laser rangefinder and sometimes IR lenses. More expensive models may include a digital camera.

lightBoosterGoogle.name: Light Booster Goggles
lightBoosterGoogle.description: Light-intensification goggles that amplify ambient light for night vision using Starlite technology. Sudden bright light can overwhelm them. With a Difficult tuning task, they can detect active IR beams.

irGoogles.name: IR Goggles
irGoogles.description: Detect hazy background infrared sources. Normally used with an active IR source for invisible illumination.

irFlash.name: IR Flashlight
irFlash.description: An active infrared light source. UV versions are similar and can be used with the proper cyberoptic.

wellDrink.name: Well Drink
wellDrink.note: restaurant or bar quality modifier applies

restaurant.name: Restaurant Meal
restaurant.note: restaurant or bar quality modifier applies

keylock.name: Keylock
keylock.description: A mechanical portal lock. Locks have four levels: Low Security (15), Medium Security (20), High Security (25) and Maximum Security (30).

cardlock.name: Cardlock
cardlock.description: An electronic portal lock using a magnetically coded card. Locks have four levels: Low Security (15), Medium Security (20), High Security (25) and Maximum Security (30).

vocolock.name: Vocolock
vocolock.description: An electronic portal lock using voice recognition. Locks have four levels: Low Security (15), Medium Security (20), High Security (25) and Maximum Security (30).

lineTap.name: Line Tap
lineTap.description: Captures voice or data from a telecommunications line for recording or retransmission. Advanced models work from about a foot away and can be remote-controlled. They do not work on systems installed or upgraded after the 2008 fiber-optic switchover.

codeDecryptor.name: Code Decryptor
codeDecryptor.description: Its probe replaces a Cardlock's normal card and adds +5 to a TECH + Electronic Security + 1D10 test against the lock.

vocDecryptor.name: VocDecryptor
vocDecryptor.description: A vocal modulator for penetrating Vocolocks.

securityScanner.name: Security Scanner
securityScanner.description: Searches for electromagnetic fields produced by alarm systems, with a 75% chance to locate one. A TECH or INT test may be needed to identify the alarm type.

poisonSniffer.name: Poison Sniffer
poisonSniffer.description: Checks air or liquid for specific poisons, or alerts the user to foreign substances. Accuracy: 85%.

jammingTransmitter.name: Jamming Transmitter
jammingTransmitter.description: Usually carried in two or three large cases, though some fill an entire van. Jams electromagnetic transmissions in a 1,000-foot area, including cellular phones and some cyberware.

scannerPlate.name: Scanner Plate
scannerPlate.description: A palmprint reader that can be attached to a Cardlock or Vocolock as an additional security layer.

movementSensor.name: Movement Sensor
movementSensor.description: An alarm system covering seismic, sonar, fixed IR or visible-light networks. Detects movement in a defined area with 95% reliability; its processor is about the size of a cigarette pack.

passCard.name: Passcard
passCard.description: The most common device used to open a Cardlock.

trackingDevice.name: Tracking Device
trackingDevice.description: Handheld or suitcase-sized equipment for detecting and following Tracer Buttons. Range: 1 mile.

tracerButton.name: Tracer Buttons
tracerButton.description: Range from matchbook-sized to pin-sized and use radioactivity or radio transmissions to reveal the position of whatever they are attached to. Some can be switched remotely.

plasKuffs.name: PlasKuffs
plasKuffs.description: Strong restraint cuffs made from modern alloys. Breaking them is Nearly Impossible; half use a Cardlock.

stripwireBlinders.name: Stripwire Binders
stripwireBlinders.description: Single-use reinforced plastic strips for temporary handcuffs and leg ties. They are Very Difficult to break, use ceramic fibers to resist cutting, and are guaranteed fireproof.

dermalStapler.name: Dermal Stapler
dermalStapler.description: Pulls the sides of a wound together and sutures them with compressed organic staples that dissolve over time.

spraySkin.name: Spray Skin
spraySkin.description: A putty-like spray gel for severe abrasions. Antiseptic, sterile and air-permeable, it flakes off in about two weeks.

slapPatch.name: Slap Patch
slapPatch.description: A small medicated plastic pad applied to the skin so the drug is absorbed in steady doses. See the Trauma Team section for drugs and prices.

criotank.name: Cryotank
criotank.description: An advanced refrigeration tank that cools a body to preservation levels while life-support maintains blood and oxygen flow, keeping a dying body in relative stasis.

medkit.name: Medkit
medkit.description: A doctor's or military corpsman's bag containing antidotes, dressings, drugs, applicators, medicines and examination instruments.

surgicalKit.name: Surgical Set
surgicalKit.description: A full set of surgical tools plus the chemicals and equipment needed to maintain a sterile operating field.

firstAidKit.name: First Aid Kit
firstAidKit.description: A household medical box containing bandages, antiseptics and a simple painkiller.

medscanner.name: Medscanner
medscanner.description: Reads body temperature, heart rate, blood pressure, respiration and blood sugar. Its chipped database grants +2 to Diagnose.

drugAnalyzer.name: Drug Analyser
drugAnalyzer.description: Ranges from book-sized to briefcase-sized. Determines the purity of known drugs or identifies the molecular structure and likely effects of substances resembling entries in its library.

airhypho.name: Airhypo
airhypho.description: Uses a burst of compressed air to force a liquid drug through the skin. See the Trauma Team section for drugs and prices.

nylonCarryBag.name: Nylon Carrybag
nylonCarryBag.description: A 2000s athletic bag or kitbag available with many logos and in various sizes.

sleepingBag.name: Sleeping Bag
sleepingBag.description: Lightweight and rated for temperatures down to -100 F. Compresses to a 12 by 6 by 4 inch bundle.

inflatableBed.name: Inflatable Bed
inflatableBed.description: A self-inflating, highly compressed mattress package measuring about 6 by 2 by 4 inches when folded.

futon.name: Futon
futon.description: A portable folding bed and pad of Japanese origin.

apartmentCube.name: Apartment Cube
apartmentCube.description: A 10 by 10 by 8 foot living module with furnishings and appliances hidden in flush wall recesses. It contains a bed, closet, stove, refrigerator, TV, digital entertainment center, two chairs, fold-down desk and removable table, and can be transported as a single unit.

lamp.name: Lamp
lamp.description: Gives light and comes in an infinity of shapes and colors.

cleaningRobot.name: Cleaning Bot
cleaningRobot.description: A small preprogrammed robotic cleaner, usually the size of a portable canister vacuum. Not very intelligent.

vocalSwitchSystem.name: Vocal Switching System
vocalSwitchSystem.description: Voice-activated controls for lights and appliances.

vehicles.name: Vehicles
vehicles.description: Typical vehicles of the early 21st century. Cybercontrols double the listed cost.

scooter.name: Scooter
scooter.description: An updated electric motorscooter with a top speed of about 50 mph and six hours of travel per fastcharge.

motorcycle.name: Motorcycle
motorcycle.description: Usually a recumbent design with protective plastic fairings. Electric models reach about 65 mph with eight hours of travel per fastcharge; CHOOH2 models reach about 140 mph with a four-gallon tank.

cityCar.name: CityCar
cityCar.description: A one-person, three-wheeled Corporate Zone car with a top speed around 40 mph and four hours per fastcharge. CityCars can also be rented from corporate-area kiosks.

smallSubcompact.name: Small Subcompact
smallSubcompact.description: Usually methanol- or CHOOH2-powered, with a top speed around 90 mph, a ten-gallon tank and four seats.

mediumSedan.name: Medium Sedan
mediumSedan.description: Methanol- or CHOOH2-powered, with a top speed around 90 mph, a fifteen-gallon tank and four seats.

sportsCar.name: Sportscar
sportsCar.description: Usually CHOOH2-powered, with a top speed around 210 mph, a ten-gallon tank and two seats.

luxurySedan.name: Luxury Sedan
luxurySedan.description: Methanol- or CHOOH2-powered, with a top speed around 90 mph, a twenty-gallon tank and six seats.

credChipAccount.name: CredChip Account
credChipAccount.description: A debit card used to carry cash electronically instead of in a wallet.

traumaTeamSilver.name: Trauma Team Silver Plan
traumaTeamSilver.note: Paramedic service; surgery billed separately; response in 1D10 turns; per month

traumaTeamGold.name: Trauma Team Gold Plan
traumaTeamGold.note: Paramedic and ambulance service with limited armed escort; surgery billed separately; response in 1D8 turns; per month

traumaTeamPlatinum.name: Trauma Team Platinum Plan
traumaTeamPlatinum.note: Paramedic, ambulance and armed escort; surgery billed separately; response in 1D6 turns; per month

traumaTeamDiamond.name: Trauma Team Diamond Plan
traumaTeamDiamond.note: Paramedic, ambulance, armed escort and cyberware repair; surgery included; response in 1D4 turns; per month

air.name: Air
air.description: In heavily polluted regions, clean air is sold by air bars, vendors, street-corner machines and stores.

kibble.name: Kibble
kibble.description: A mass-produced nutrient satisfying most dietary needs but resembling dry pet food in look, smell and taste.

genericPrepak.name: Generic Prepak
genericPrepak.description: A basic packaged meal that can be microwaved or refrigerated. Many include chemical heating or cooling tabs.

goodPrepak.name: Good Prepak
goodPrepak.description: A good restaurant meal in a package, representing the best commonly available pre-made food.

freshFood.name: Fresh Food
freshFood.description: Actual fresh food, or at least something eaten by someone who has seen it.

coffin.name: Coffin
coffin.description: A stacked, coin-operated sleeping box found in airports and flophouses. It has just enough room to turn around or read in bed; expensive models may include a phone or mini-TV.

apartment.name: Apartment/Condo
apartment.note: per room, per month; location modifier applies

house.name: House
house.note: per room, per month; location modifier applies
